invariant_audit.subject: logging never breaks a tool call
evidence: log-tool-calls.sh uses set +e so no shell error propagates a blocking exit code to Claude Code
python3 guard (b55f17d): command -v python3 || exit 0 at line 22 of log-tool-calls.sh silently no-ops when python3 is absent
explicit OSError return (96981e4): log_tool_call.py lines 208-215 catch ALL OSError variants (ENOSPC, EACCES, EROFS, etc.) and return 0, not just ENOSPC
_log_core refactor (e689246): patterns/truncation/atomic_append consolidated into _log_core.py; log_tool_call.py imports them directly — no subprocess pipeline that could fail mid-chain
top-level exception guard in log_tool_call.py (lines 219-224): except Exception: sys.exit(0) catches all runtime errors that escape main()
log-tool-calls.sh uses exec python3 ... so the python3 exit code is directly the hook exit code — no intermediate shell error handling needed

findings.title: Module-level ImportError in log_tool_call.py not guarded by top-level try/except
findings.detail: from _log_core import ... executes at module load time, before the if __name__ == __main__ block and its except Exception: sys.exit(0) guard. If _log_core.py is missing, corrupt, or has a syntax error, Python exits with code 1 (ImportError traceback). exec python3 in log-tool-calls.sh propagates that exit code directly to Claude Code. On PreToolUse, exit code 1 is non-blocking per Claude Code semantics so no tool call is actually broken, but the session produces noisy hook-error messages and logging silently stops for the duration.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the module-level import in a try/except at the top of the if __name__ == __main__ block, or use a lazy import inside main(), so the existing except Exception: sys.exit(0) guard covers import failures. Alternatively, wrap the entire module body in a top-level try/except BaseException.

fixes_verified.verdict: CORRECT — command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0 fires before exec, ensuring the hook exits 0 (not 127) when python3 is absent

fixes_verified.description: explicit OSError return 0 for all OSError variants in log_tool_call.py
fixes_verified.verdict: CORRECT — except OSError as exc: ... return 0 now catches EACCES, EROFS, and all other OSError variants, not only ENOSPC. The _ = exc acknowledgment makes the swallow intentional and lint-visible.

fixes_verified.description: _log_core refactor: single source of truth for patterns + truncation + atomic_append
fixes_verified.verdict: CORRECT — _log_core.py is the canonical definition; redact.py, jsonl_write.py, and log_tool_call.py all import from it. The bash-based subprocess pipeline (redact.py | jsonl_write.py) is eliminated from the hook path. log-tool-calls.sh now execs a single python3 process.

residual_risks.description: jsonl_write.py CLI still returns exit 1 for non-ENOSPC OSErrors. This is no longer in the hook pipeline, but if someone invokes it directly (e.g., in a custom script or future hook), a permission error on the log file would surface as exit 1 rather than silent drop.
residual_risks.actionability: Document in the file docstring that the exit-1-on-non-ENOSPC behavior is intentional for CLI use; differs from log_tool_call.py which swallows all OSErrors.

residual_risks.description: log-rotate.sh gzip rotation is non-atomic (gzip -c > dest && rm src). A crash between write and rm leaves a corrupt .gz alongside the original. Already tracked as issue #7.

testing_gaps.description: No test exercises the ImportError scenario for log_tool_call.py (e.g., temporarily renaming _log_core.py and asserting log-tool-calls.sh exits 0 and does not block the tool call). The python3-guard is tested but the import-failure path is not.
